the Ca(2+) concentration dependent fluorescence intensity changes in cameleons arise from a combination of the following effects: (1) a decrease of the fluorescence quantum yield of the donor upon Ca(2+), binding; (2) a change of the energy transfer efficiency from the donor to the acceptor; and (3) a change in the donor fluorescence decay time.
The main takeaway from our work is that

time-resolved fluorescence spectroscopy is a powerful method to investigate conformational changes in cameleons upon Ca(2+ binding and to obtain quantitative information on the energy-transfer efficiency, rate constants, and distances between the donor and acceptor in the Ca( 2+)-free, Ca(2+ )-bound, and Ca(2+) saturated samples.
